meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to look', forming an aspectual pair with 'посмотреть'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to watch') (TV, a film) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('leather').

examples.trans: Look, this is a leather belt.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'belt', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: A leather strap on the watch.

examples.text: Пожалуйста, не затягивайте ремень слишком сильно.
examples.trans: Please do not tighten the strap too tightly.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'what for'.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('long').

examples.trans: Are the pants too long for Slavik?
Which dish travels a long way?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to prepare', forming an aspectual pair with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ъесть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to eat', forming an aspectual pair with 'есть'.

examples.text: Скоро. А пока я есть хочу, слона бы съел!
examples.trans: Soon. But for now I'm hungry, I could eat an elephant!

meanings.note: needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
not to be confused with есть 'there is' (from быть)

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to prepare') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to have a look', forming an aspectual pair with 'смотреть'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to watch (a film) through') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: predicative: очень вкусно = it's delicious
Secondary conversational sense ('deliciously') (вкусно готовить = to cook well) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian preposition meaning 'until' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('goodbye') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Declinable feminine noun meaning 'meeting', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('see you') (in 'до встречи' = until we meet) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?
